G.lives: herb-lore of the wood's witch, but walled, tidy and tame

H.lives: the old tales carried from earlier tellers; the wildness itself is absent

I.lives: the old tales and their tellers, handed down from those who came before

J.lives: a lantern carried into the dark wood, brave enough to go in

K.lives: seasonal folk lore and herbs, recorded like tables; the wild part is absent

L.lives: old tales read by night under one lamp; the wildness stays on the page

M.lives: a tale opening 'once upon a time', winking at the comic panel

note: The margins are where the wild creatures crowd the ink and borders, clever and a little dangerous, and the page stays hers to fill.
